News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Trump urges voters to let GOP ‘finish the job’ in midterm convention speech

DALLAS — President Trump headlined the Republican Party’s first-ever midterm convention Wednesday night, boasting about his record and offering every American $5,000 if Republicans hold control of Congress in the Nov. 3 election.

Trump implored listeners to “pretend that I’m on the ballot” so he can “finish the job” —presenting a stark choice between “radical left communists” and a continuation of his populist agenda.

The president offered Americans a major financial incentive to stick with him in what he called the “best part” of his energetic barnstorming-style 107-minute speech.

“If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them, because of our tremendous economic success… I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000,” Trump said.

It’s unclear if the idea would pass muster with fiscal conservatives — as it would add more than $1.2 trillion to the already surging $40 trillion national debt.

In 2020, then-Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) blocked Trump’s request for $2,000 COVID-19 stimulus checks and made the sum $600 due to fear that printing so much money would devalue the currency.

President Joe Biden later approved the additional $1,400 — with critics saying it fueled an inflation crisis, which peaked at an annual rate of 9.1% in June 2022.

Two South Florida men are behind bars this week after federal prosecutors proved they turned durable medical equipment into a $34.8 million heist against American seniors. “𝘛𝘩𝘦𝘴𝘦 𝘧𝘳𝘢𝘶𝘥𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘦𝘥 𝘔𝘦𝘥𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘦 $34.8 𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘣𝘳𝘢𝘤𝘦𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘱𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘴 𝘥𝘪𝘥𝘯'𝘵 𝘯𝘦𝘦𝘥,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald — and a federal judge made sure Kenneth Kessler and Michael Gomez paid for it with their freedom.

Kessler, 43, of Miami, and Gomez, 43, of Miramar, ran seven durable medical equipment companies that existed for one purpose: siphoning taxpayer money out of Medicare. Court records show the pair 𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐝 𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐥 𝐤𝐢𝐜𝐤𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐟𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐝𝐨𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐬' 𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬, then shipped back, knee, shoulder, and ankle braces to Medicare beneficiaries nationwide who never asked for them and never needed them. When one shell company's Medicare payments got suspended for suspicious billing, they simply shifted the fraud to the next one and kept the checks coming.

The scam moved fast enough that Kessler personally pocketed $1.4 million and Gomez walked away with $2.3 million before investigators caught up. In May, both men pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit health care fraud; on September 4, a federal judge handed Kessler 33 months and Gomez 24 months in federal prison — real time, not probation, for stealing from a program seniors paid into their entire working lives.

CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, who's made rooting out Medicare fraud a signature mission, pointed to the case live on air as proof the crackdown isn't just talk. “𝘛𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘪𝘴 𝘫𝘶𝘴𝘵 𝘢𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘦𝘹𝘢𝘮𝘱𝘭𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘦𝘹𝘢𝘮𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘳𝘢𝘤𝘬𝘥𝘰𝘸𝘯 𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘳𝘢𝘶𝘥. 𝘐𝘵'𝘴 𝘩𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘪𝘯𝘨,” Oz told Fox News from the studio where the network broke the sentencing news to viewers.

9 PM Top-of-the-Hour News

While the room was chock full of Republicans for tonight's Midterm convention, there were SOME Democrats making their presence known, even if only by video message.: “A big room of Republicans in Dallas. Yes, I'm Senator John Fetterman, Pennsylvania. Yes, I'm a Democrat. Why am I here talking to you today? Because, well, I'm a common sense Democrat. I'm always gonna stand with America. ”
Speakers include Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Attorney General Todd Blanche, Dr. Mehmet Oz, and Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton. Of Course President Trump is headlining the event.

Illinois Governor J-B Pritzker slammed Republicans for what he says are efforts to suppress voting in Texas and the rest of the county ahead of the Republican midterm convention in Texas.: “They're trying to take health care away from people. They're trying to take food assistance away from people. Uh, they're succeeding in a lot of cases. They're attacking people in our streets, in our American cities. They want to send troops into American cities. Apparently, the Republican Congress, led by mega Republicans, uh, are OK with everything that Donald Trump is doing. ”
Pritzker is part of counter programming by Democrats planned for the convention.

The U S and Iran continue to trade strikes in the middle east. NewsNation's Robert Sherman reports: “What you've seen in the last 24 hours, American forces striking Iranian tankers. This is the new American position. If you target US naval vessels here in the region, well, Iranian tankers will be hit to put added pressure on Iran's economy, but Iran still. Demonstrates the ability and the capability to retaliate and to touch regions around the Middle East. Here. What we saw overnight, the skies above Jordan lit up with Iranian ballistic missiles fired at American service members stationed in Jordan. ”

SPOT PLATINUM SURGED 5% ON WEDNESDAY, BREAKING ABOVE $1,900/OZ TO A 14-WEEK HIGH.

At the same time, the World Platinum Investment Council ($WPIC) released its Q2 2026 $Platinum Quarterly, forecasting a full-year market surplus of 8 tonnes (265,000 ounces) - a sharp reversal from its previous deficit projection.

WPIC Quarterly Report - Key takeaways

Full-Year 2026 Forecast Reversal:

· Surplus of 8 tonnes (265,000 oz) - versus the previous forecast of a 297,000 oz deficit

· Total supply: 229 tonnes (+2%), driven by higher recycling

· Total demand: 220 tonnes (-18%), primarily due to a sharp drop in investment demand

Q2 Data:

· Quarterly surplus of 8 tonnes - the second consecutive quarterly surplus

· Supply: 1.906M oz; Demand: 1.663M oz - a 244,000 oz surplus

· Platinum $ETF outflows of 7 tonnes drove net investment of 4 tonnes

WPIC Head of Research Ed Sterck:
"The platinum market recorded a 548,000 oz surplus in H1 2026, driven almost entirely by investment liquidation - nearly 600,000 oz flowed out of ETFs and exchange inventories."

However, he stressed that the market is set to return to a 283,000 oz deficit in H2, as "selling has stopped and buying is returning."

The Root of H1 selling - A macro shock

WPIC attributed the collapse in investment demand to the Middle East conflict pushing oil prices higher, which in turn drove up inflation expectations and caused markets to pivot from pricing "two rate cuts" to "two rate hikes" from the Fed.

Platinum prices plunged over 46% from their January all-time high of $2,875/oz, with ETF holdings declining by more than 500,000 oz (roughly one-seventh of end-2025 holdings).

Despite the full-year surplus forecast, WPIC sees fundamentals as still relatively tight:

· Above-ground inventories are critically depleted - after three consecutive years of significant deficits, even an 8-tonne surplus in 2026 would cover only 3.4 months of global demand

· Industrial demand up 5%, offsetting a 4% decline in automotive demand

· Jewellery demand expected to fall 15%, weighed down by high prices and weak Chinese consumption

WPIC CEO Trevor Raymond noted that platinum's strategic importance continues to grow, particularly in AI and data center infrastructure.

Near-term price driver:
Spot platinum surged 5% on Wednesday to $1,904–1,910/oz, hitting a 14-week high as markets priced in the H2 deficit narrative and the return of the debasement trade.

Long-term structural tension:
A modest full-year surplus (8 tonnes) vs. critically depleted above-ground inventories (3.4 months of coverage) vs. a return to deficit in H2 (283,000 oz) - the platinum market is at a delicate inflection point.

WPIC's conclusion:
Platinum offers a higher-beta alternative to gold in the debasement trade.

quote:
ChatGPTに毎回、自分の仕事を説明していませんか。
私は会社をひとりで回しています。戦略も、調査も、資料づくりも、予定管理も、全部自分。AIは毎日使っていましたが、正直に言うと「効率化の道具」止まりでした。文章を短くしてもらう。メールの下書きを作ってもらう。便利ではあるけれど、仕事の相棒とは呼べない。
理由ははっきりしています。普通のAIチャットは、会話が終わればあなたを忘れるからです。優秀な新人が、毎朝記憶を失って出社してくるようなもの。どれだけ丁寧に説明しても、明日はまたゼロから。履歴は流れ、先週の続きはできない。資料も読ませられない。問題はAIの性能ではなく、「記憶と文脈の置き場所」が無いことでした。
そこで発想を変えました。「AIを使う」のではなく、「参謀組織を持つ」。
いま私のPCの中には、作戦室と呼んでいるフォルダがひとつあります。この部屋に記憶も、資料も、成果物も、すべて蓄積されます。そして、そこで5つの役割の参謀が働いています。
・筆頭参謀——戦略の壁打ち相手。整理する→決める→動く、の順で意思決定を支える ・秘書官——毎朝、目標から「今日のTOP3」を理由つきで提案する ・情報参謀——調べものを引き受けて、レポートにして返す ・制作参謀——私の資料をもとに、企画書や提案書を作る ・記録官——今日の決定と成果を記録し、明日は「昨日の続き」から始めさせる
種明かしをすると、司令塔は1つのAIです。その配下に「秘書」「調査」「制作」の3つの専門エージェントが定義されていて、仕事の内容に応じて自動で呼び分けられます。大げさなマルチAIシステムではありません。だから軽く、迷わず、管理するのはフォルダひとつだけ。
一日の流れは、こうです。朝、パソコンを開いて「今日やること決めて」と一言。秘書官が昨日の記録を踏まえたTOP3を理由つきで出してくる。思いついたことは「覚えておいて」のひと言で記録官へ。午後は情報参謀の調査レポートを眺めながら、筆頭参謀と次の一手を壁打ちする。夕方に「今日をまとめて」で締めると、翌朝はその続きから始まります。コマンドを覚える必要はなく、全部ふつうの日本語で通じます。
一番効いたのは、資料を入れるフォルダです。会社案内、事業計画、過去のブログ。眠っていた10年分の資料を入れておくと、それがそのまま参謀の頭脳になります。「私の過去の資料を参考に、新しい企画を考えて」が通る。返ってくるのは一般論ではなく、自分の文脈を踏まえた提案です。AIに答えを聞くのではなく、AIと一緒に自分の答えをつくる。この違いは、体験すると戻れません。
もうひとつ大事にしているのは、采配は自分が振ることです。資料は読み取り専用。送信・購入・削除は必ず本人の承認。記憶はすべて自分のPCの中に残ります。参謀は準備し、進言する。決めるのは、いつも自分。AIに仕事を任せるのが怖かった私でも、この設計なら安心して預けられました。
ひとりで決め続けるコストは、意外と高いと思っています。判断は遅れ、選択肢は狭まり、誰にも壁打ちできないまま走り出してしまう。必要だったのは「もっと優秀なAI」ではなく、自分の文脈を覚えていて、役割分担してくれる組織でした。
この仕組みは「OZ AI Strategic Navigator」という名前で、誰でも開いた日から使える形に磨き直しています。導入は3ステップ・約15分。フォルダを開いて、7つの質問に答えるだけ。設定ファイルは1文字も書きません。
ひとりで決めるのは、今日で終わり。続報はプロフィールと固定ポストでお知らせします。

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.
As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.
As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

quote:
FREEPORT $FCX IS SELLING 30% LESS COPPER INTO A RECORD PRICE:

Freeport-McMoRan FCX at $76.44 (after hours), +$3.71 / +5.10%. It closed the regular session at $76.62, +$3.89 / +5.35%. The Phoenix company mines copper in Arizona and New Mexico, in Peru and Chile, and at the Grasberg district in Indonesia.

The verdict: copper set an all-time high today partly because Freeport is not shipping enough of it. That makes the record a thinner prize for this company than the headline reads, and it puts the next leg here on pounds rather than on the metal going higher.

The record is real. Comex December copper futures at $6.844 a pound, +$0.16 / +2.41%, an all-time high. On the London Metal Exchange, which prices copper by the tonne, three-month copper reached $14,703 a metric ton, +$189 / +1.3% - a second record session in a row.

Now the tell. The metal made a new high today. The miner did not. Freeport's close is 4.5% under the $80.24 it printed on August 26. It ran to $78.64 intraday, +8.1% on the day, then gave back about a third of that before the bell, on 16.7M shares against days near 13.9M.

One idea explains the gap. A miner earns price times pounds, and the halves do not always move together. When copper rises because the world wants more, a miner wins twice: it ships more tonnes and each one fetches more. When copper rises because mines are failing, the miner that failed collects the better price on a smaller pile. Same headline, very different payday.

Freeport is the second case, and its own last report says so. The June quarter, published July 23:

- Copper sold 710M lb vs 1,016M lb a year earlier, down 30%
- Gold sold 123k oz vs 522k oz
- Revenue $7.03B vs $7.58B, down 7%
- Profit $984M, or $0.68 a share; $0.74 once $96M of costs tied to the accident below come out
- Average price received $6.17 a pound, against $4.75 across the whole of 2025
- Unit net cash costs - what it spends to get one pound out of the ground and to a customer - $1.97 a pound, leaving $4.20 of cash margin on every pound it did sell
- Cash from operations $2.0B; cash $4.1B against $9.4B of total borrowings

Read the first three lines together. Freeport sold 30% fewer pounds of copper and 76% fewer ounces of gold, and revenue fell 7%. Price covered nearly the whole hole - which is also the measure of how much volume is gone.

It is gone for a dated reason, and the date is today. On September 8, 2025, roughly 800,000 tonnes of wet material flowed through the openings where ore is drawn out of one production block at the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine in Indonesia, and drained into the levels below. Seven miners were killed. Freeport halted the mine and told customers it could not deliver. A phased restart began in the June quarter of this year.

Everything published since is a line down. On January 22 Freeport mapped 3.4B lb of copper sales for 2026. By July that map read about 3.1B. It actually sold 3.6B lb in 2025. Put a size on the 500M lb gap between last year and this year's plan: about 227,000 metric tons, close to half of the roughly 475,000 tonnes J.P. Morgan expects every AI data centre on earth to consume in 2026.

The fair counter is a strong one: this shortage is not Freeport's to end. The International Copper Study Group put global copper mine production down 1.1% in the first half of this year, which would make 2026 the first annual decline since 2017. Chile, which mines about a quarter of the world's copper, had its weakest second quarter in at least 19 years and cut its official full-year forecast a second time, to a 2.6% decline. Grasberg coming back does not hand the price back. It means Freeport collects on more of it.

So the case sits on one number: pounds against that 3.1B map. Freeport says the Grasberg Block Cave runs near 65% of capacity across the back half of this year, 80% by the middle of 2027, and close to full by the end of 2027. The price has already improved on the last report - $6.844 today is about 11% above the $6.17 that quarter banked. Margin is not the question. Tonnage is.

Freeport is not a current pick on any of the six Len5es, and the near miss is the instructive part. Deep-Value and Special-Situations watches a genuinely good business marked down after something visible and dated went wrong, and the went-wrong half could hardly be better settled. The marked-down half fails: $76.62 is 118% above the $35.15 of September 25 last year, near 36 times earnings and about 5.2 times book value - roughly what would be left after selling up and paying everyone off. Paying 36 times for a miner while its metal sits at a record is the wrong end of that trade, not a discount. Two or three quarters of full-rate output to value against, or a real fall in the price with the restart on schedule, is what would change it.

One peer sharpens it. Southern Copper closed at $208.60, +$9.84 / +4.95% today. Same metal, Peru and Mexico, no accident - so it gets both halves of today. It fits none of the six styles either, for the opposite reason: near 13 times book value leaves no gap between price and worth for a value style to work with.

The risk is the half nobody at Freeport sets. Copper averaged $4.75 a pound across 2025, and back at that level the restart does not save this - and part of the dividend goes too, $0.15 a quarter, about 0.8% of the price a year, half of it a variable piece that moves with the metal.

Freeport has not dated the September quarter; the last two landed July 23 and January 22, both before the open, and outside calendars put this one in the second half of October. That report is the first place anyone can check the pounds.

A record price only pays on the tonnage you have to sell into it. Freeport got the best copper price ever printed today and still closed under its own August high, because what is being bought here is not the metal - it is a mine that does not run at full rate until the end of 2027.

Asian Session Wrap - Tuesday, September 8

Asian markets traded mixed but mostly higher on Tuesday, with chip and A.I. stocks powering sharp gains in Tokyo and Seoul, while Hong Kong lagged on weakness in tech and biopharma.

The region's divergence reflects a clear theme:
A.I. hardware is leading, while broader China exposure is dragging.

Equities - Chips lead, KOSPI breaks 7,000

🇰🇷 South Korea: KOSPI surged 4.61% to 6,995.39, driven by chip stocks. Samsung Electronics soared 5.7% and SK Hynix surged 8.1% .
The index briefly broke above 7,000 intraday before paring - a 15-month high.

🇯🇵 Japan: Nikkei 225 added 2.1% to 66,399.84, its best session in weeks. Tokyo Electron +4.7%, Renesas +3.1%, Rohm +7.8%. The AI hardware trade remains the "most dependable growth pulse."

🇭🇰 Hong Kong: Hang Seng fell 0.85% to 25,431.58, weighed down by tech and biopharma weakness. Optical comms and storage concepts gained, but property and auto stocks sold off.

🇨🇳 China: Shanghai Composite rose 0.07% to 3,932.70; Shenzhen Component surged 1.91% and ChiNext jumped 3.41% on AI and tech strength.

🇦🇺 Australia: S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.7% to ~9,010 - underperforming on weak Westpac Consumer Sentiment and NAB Business Confidence surveys.

🇸🇬 Singapore - STI eased 0.17%.

FX - Yen surges, Dollar breaks 99

USDJPY plunged to 153.496, down over 1% - its strongest level since February, driven by BoJ rate hike expectations. Markets are pricing a ~99% probability of a September 18 hike, with some expecting rates to hit 1.25% .

DXY fell below $99 to $98.91 - a 0.26% drop.

USDCNY fix set at 6.7804, down 9 pips. 100
JPYCNY surged 608 pips to 4.3706 - reflecting yen strength.

EURUSD: 1.163 - up 0.07%
AUDUSD: 0.721 - down 0.05%
GBPUSD: 1.354 - up 0.03%

Commodities - Copper Hits Record, Oil Surges

Copper - LME copper hit a fresh all-time high of $14,533/ton on U.S. tariff expectations, extending gains for a third session.

Crude Oil - Brent settled 1.1% higher at $97.31/bbl, reaching 92.65/bbl**.

Gold - Spot gold traded around $4,400/oz as traders weighed oil-driven inflation against a stronger yen.

The Main Event: CPI on Friday is the absolute focus, if it surprises higher, September Fed hike odds will jump; if it cools, doves get the upper hand.

The Fed's September 16 meeting has a ~60% probability of a 25bp hike priced in following the blowout 162K NFP print.

Verdict

Three themes dominated Asian trading:

1. A.I. hardware is the undisputed leader. KOSPI surged 4.6%, Nikkei 2.1% - chip stocks are the region's most dependable growth pulse.

2. The yen is surging. USDJPY broke below ¥154 on ~99% BoJ hike expectations, but a stronger yen is a headwind for Japan's export-driven equities.

3. Geopolitical risk is rising. Brent hit $97 on
U.S.-Iran attacks and Saudi facility strikes, keeping inflation fears front and center.

1. 🛢️ US-Iran Conflict Escalates – Oil Approaches $98

Over the weekend, the US and Iran exchanged attacks on oil tankers and naval vessels. The US struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday; Iran responded by firing ballistic missiles at two US destroyers. Iran's parliamentary speaker declared "the era of symmetrical responses is over" and announced plans to establish a new "restricted zone" from the Strait of Hormuz to the US naval blockade line. On Monday, Saudi Aramco's Jizan refinery was hit by an attack — responsibility remains unclear.

Goldman Sachs raised its year-end Brent forecast to $85/bbl.

💬 : The US-Iran conflict has escalated from "maritime skirmishes" to an "economic war" — commercial shipping is being deliberately weaponized by both sides. The dollar index lost the 99 level, closing -0.26% at 98.91. USD/JPY approached 154, hitting its lowest since February 23, down over 1% on the day. The yen has fully reversed its July 40-year lows.

Markets are almost fully pricing a 25bp BOJ rate hike to 1.25% in September. Japan's wage growth hit its fastest pace since 1997, reinforcing rate hike expectations.

Asian markets diverged sharply — KOSPI surged 4.61% to 6,995, Nikkei 225 +2.12%. The GPT-6 AI model release ignited semiconductor and storage chip demand expectations across Japan and Korea. A-shares saw the ChiNext Index +3.41%, while Hong Kong closed -0.93% on local stock weakness.

💬 : The yen's surge is reshaping global carry trade dynamics. Rising BOJ rate expectations and narrowing US-Japan yield differentials are accelerating the trend. Asian chip stocks surging shows markets repricing AI compute demand.

3. 🛢️ Copper Hits All-Time High, Gold Consolidates Near $4,400

LME copper broke above $14,533/ton, hitting an all-time high.

**Spot gold closed -0.54% at $4,406.44/oz**, hitting as low as $4,381 intraday. A weaker dollar failed to lift gold, with rate-hike expectations capping safe-haven demand.

💬 : Copper and AI chip stocks rallying in tandem — capital is flowing into the "AI infrastructure" trade. Gold remains caught between rate expectations and geopolitical risk.

🔥 Big Picture

US-Iran escalation + yen surge + AI frenzy — three narratives simultaneously driving global asset pricing.

Three transmission chains running simultaneously:

US-Iran tanker attacks + Saudi Aramco refinery hit → Brent approaches $98 → Hormuz traffic at 5-month lows → geopolitical premium burning hot

quote:
Happy Labor Day:
What has President Trump done for America in just this past week?

Here is a partial list.

Please share.
 He is accomplishing so much; even our people have difficulty keeping t Most Favored Nation Drug Pricing Set to Save Americans $600 Billion, 162,000 New Jobs Created in August, Two Executive Orders Back America’s Ranchers, and Operation Economic Outcast Expands to a Global Coalition

On this Labor Day — the holiday honoring the American worker — President Trump delivered a landmark win for every family in the country. On August 31, the President announced a new round of Most Favored Nation drug pricing agreements, projected to save Americans an estimated $600 billion on prescription drugs. Participating manufacturers — including Bayer, Takeda, and CSL — now align their U.S. prices with the lowest prices charged in other high-income nations such as Canada, Japan, and European countries. https://t.co/rPCrE1K9SK covers approximately 80% of commonly dispensed pharmacy medications, and the most recent data confirmed the steepest annual prescription drug price decline in more than 60 years. As Dr. Mehmet Oz noted, one in three Americans previously walked out of the pharmacy empty-handed because they couldn’t afford their medication. That era is ending.

The August jobs report delivered a blockbuster number that shocked Wall Street economists who had expected far less: 162,000 new jobs created — nearly triple the consensus forecast. President Trump’s second term has now produced more than 1 million private-sector jobs. Manufacturing posted its strongest monthly gain in three years, adding 16,000 positions driven by demand for pharmaceutical, defense, and semiconductor production. Construction added 22,000 jobs, with factory construction up nearly 100,000 since inauguration day. Average private-sector weekly earnings rose 3.7% year-over-year, and Black unemployment posted its second consecutive monthly decline.

On September 2, the White House released the official accounting of the biggest oil deal in world history, detailing the full scope of the agreement securing majority U.S. governance rights, economic ownership, and guaranteed low-cost off-take of 65+ billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela. The private company operating those fields currently produces 250,000 barrels per day and will rank among the world’s largest private oil companies by reserves. Material production is expected by early 2027, with at-cost deliveries to the United States projected to lower gas prices by year-end. The administration frames the deal as direct enforcement of the Monroe Doctrine — cutting off foreign adversary influence in the Western Hemisphere while securing American energy dominance for the next century, at zero cost to the taxpayer.

On September 4, President Trump signed two executive orders to defend America’s ranchers and break the chokehold on the nation’s beef supply. The first — Supporting America’s Ranchers — directs Interior to evaluate delisting gray and Mexican wolves under the Endangered Species Act, updates predator compensation standards, and initiates a review of beef labeling to ensure consumers know where their beef was raised. The second — Promoting Fair Competition in Livestock Markets — targets the alarming consolidation in beef processing: the four largest packers now control approximately 85% of all steer and heifer purchases, up from just 36% four decades ago. The order mandates aggressive Packers and Stockyards Act enforcement, expands interstate market access for small and regional processors, and creates a new loan program for independent processing facilities.

Operation Economic Outcast — the administration’s maximum-pressure campaign against Iran — is evolving from a U.S. operation into a global coalition. The European Union has now joined U.S. sanctions, and South Korea is weighing direct military backing of the Strait of Hormuz blockade. On September 2, U.S. forces conducted their most significant single-day operation since the blockade began: 60 Iranian targets struck and 18 million barrels of oil protected in a single day — a record that underscores the escalating scale and precision of American operations. Iran continues to lose an estimated $13 billion per month in oil revenue, with no relief in sight.

ICE launched “Operation Rotten Apple "across New York, arresting more than 2,000 illegal migrants — including convicted child rapists and murderers — in a sweeping enforcement action that confirms the reach of maximum enforcement into even the most politically resistant jurisdictions. The State Department announced the launch of a Foundry School to train the skilled manufacturing workforce behind America’s industrial comeback. The United States struck a light-touch AI regulation accord with G20 members at the Innovation Ministerial, establishing America’s preferred global framework and preventing the regulatory overreach that could slow American technological leadership. And Delta Airlines announced it will match the federal government’s $1,000 Trump Account seed money for children, with a growing list of American companies pledging similar contributions.

President Trump called the International Space Station from Mission Control in a live conversation with American astronauts — a vivid symbol of America’s renewed space leadership and this administration’s personal investment in the men and women who fly for this nation. First Lady Melania Trump completed her 34th family reunification of children displaced by the Russia-Ukraine war, bringing more young people home to their families in a humanitarian mission conducted quietly and consistently across her tenure. As Americans celebrate this Labor Day, the results speak for themselves: drug prices falling at their fastest pace in 60 years, manufacturing booming, the beef monopoly being broken, Iran under maximum pressure, and the United States having secured the biggest oil deal in world history.

Asian Markets: Japan, South Korea Extend Gains; Mainland China and Hong Kong Weaken

Tuesday's Asian market opening showed clear divergence. Japan's $Nikkei 225 opened up 0.9%, extending Monday's 1.9%–2.2% rally. South Korea's $KOSPI, however, opened sharply down 2.58%, with both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix falling over 3% – a stark reversal from Monday's 3.37% surge.

Mainland China and Hong Kong markets continued to struggle – on Monday, the Shanghai Composite fell 0.24%, the Hang Seng Index dropped 0.97%, while the Shenzhen market bucked the trend with a 1.3% gain. India's Nifty 50 slipped 0.25%, and Australia's ASX 200 was nearly flat.

Chip stocks have been this week's main theme: On Monday, SK Hynix jumped 8.1% and Samsung Electronics rose 4.7%, driven by optimism over AI chip demand from OpenAI's new model. But in Tuesday pre‑market, SK Hynix had already tumbled about 8%, indicating that the sell‑off in U.S. chip stocks is spilling over to Asia.

U.S. markets were closed Monday for the Labor Day holiday.

On Friday (September 4), all three major U.S. indices ended lower:

· Dow: -0.51%, closing at 53,414.25
· S&P 500: -0.38%, closing at 7,718.60
· Nasdaq: -0.29%, closing at 26,506.99

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index bucked the trend, surging 3.37%, led by memory and optical communications stocks. Tesla fell 5.92%.

The main driver for the decline was the August non‑farm payrolls report – which came in at 162,000 new jobs (vs. expectations of just 56,000), causing rate‑hike expectations to heat up sharply.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy claimed it struck three oil tankers and several U.S.‑affiliated vessels. This follows earlier U.S. strikes on Iranian tankers. Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary announced that a "no‑go zone" will be established in the Strait of Hormuz in the coming days.

Oil prices jumped in response:

· Brent crude hit $97.1/barrel
· WTI crude broke above $93/barrel

The U.S. Energy Secretary stated that the U.S. "may have to destroy Iran's nuclear capabilities."

FX & Commodities

· Dollar Index: $99.177

· USDJPY: around 154.4, having previously rebounded from 155.50 to 156.22

· Offshore yuan: around 6.71

· Spot gold: rebounded to above $4,429/oz
(Friday's close was $4,429)

· WTI crude: above 96–97/bbl

Early 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

News Flashback

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

I am incredibly grateful to the teams behind Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, and Gemini. Combined with my 20+ years of experience in enterprise web security and web development, these coding agents made it possible for me to build at a pace I would never have imagined a few years ago.

In just 18 months, I proved something to myself:

Almost anything is possible with software when you clearly understand the problem you are trying to solve.

If something is repetitive, boring, time-consuming, unnecessarily expensive, or frustrating to use, I now ask a simple question:

Can this be simplified with an app or a business platform that others can use too?

That thinking led to a portfolio of applications and platforms, each built around a specific problem:

AisleSeeker — A privacy-first retail product-finding platform designed to help shoppers locate items quickly inside stores. I redesigned its original AI mechanism into a deterministic-first architecture using keyword triggers and structured store data, so common requests can be answered without paying for an AI API call every time. 投資需要は堅調を維持する一方、ジュエリー需要は高値疲れで前年比-9%超に縮小しそう。
データセンターやAI・EV向けの工業需要が下支えになってるって話。

▶ パースミント、8月の金貨・金地金販売が+38%（Perth Mint、2026-09-06）
パースミントの8月販売は金貨・金バー合わせて30,125オンス。
前月の21,891オンスから+38%増えたみたい。

馬年のルナシリーズへの先行予約が効いてる感じで、8月の金相場も+4.8%と4月以来の月間成績だった。
銀は8月末に14年ぶり高値をつけたのに、パースミントの銀販売はまさかの8か月ぶり低水準。

▶ 利上げ観測70%まで急伸、金は年間の上げ幅ほぼ帳消しに（https://t.co/BQkyP0ema0、2026-09-06）
一時はFRBの9月利上げ観測が70%まで上がって、金は2026年の上昇分をほぼ失った。
銀も同時に下げてる。

その後ウォーラー理事が「インフレ鈍化が続けば据え置き支持」と発言して、確率は50%前後まで戻したみたい。
米10年債利回りは4.79%まで上昇してた。

▶ 金スポット、週間で4,325〜4,500ドルの荒い値動き（LBMA、2026-09-06）
LBMAの金スポット価格は9月5日時点で4,443.53ドル。
週間レンジは4,325〜4,500ドル付近とかなり広かった。

強い雇用統計を受けた利上げ観測と、ウォーラー理事の発言による反発が交錯して、荒れた1週間だったみたい。

▶ 金、4,350ドルの節目を試す展開に（Kitco News、2026-09-05）
Kitcoによると、金は8月に+10%上昇したあと9月に入って反落し、4,429ドルで4,350ドルのサポートを試してる。
WGCは「財務省とFRBのシグナルが錯綜していて、金には総じてマイナス」とコメントしたらしい。
9月の利上げ観測は60%まで上がっていて、戻りは限定的になりそうって見方だった。

▶ オランダ中銀、金86トンをNYからロンドンへ移送（Northern Miner、2026-09-06）
オランダ中央銀行が金86トンをニューヨーク連銀からロンドンへ移した。
これで北米での保管比率は31%から19%まで下がったみたい。

有事の際のアクセス確保が狙いらしくて、欧州の中央銀行がアメリカ離れを進めてる動きとして注目されてる。

▶ 中央銀行の金購入、7月は半分以上減少（Northern Miner、2026-09-06）
7月の世界の中央銀行による金購入量が、前月比で半分以上減ったことがわかった。
金相場が記録的な高値圏にある中での鈍化なので、けっこう気になる数字。

公的セクターの購入が落ち着いてくると、これからは民間投資家の需要が価格サポートの主役になっていくのかもしれない。

▶ 「押し目はすぐ買い戻される」、強気トレンド継続との見方（Adrian Day、2026-09-06）
エイドリアン・デイは、金の下落局面はすぐに買い戻されていて上昇トレンドはまだ終わってないとみてる。
中央銀行によるドル準備削減や実物資産へのシフトが主なサポートらしい。

JPモルガンは年末6,000ドルを予測していて、9月の想定レンジは4,136〜5,304ドルとかなり幅広い。

▶ BOJ、9月18日会合で追加利上げ有力に（Bank of Japan Statistics、2026-09-06）
日銀は9月18日の会合で+0.25%の追加利上げが有力視されてるみたい。
高田審議委員は機動的な利上げを支持していて、半期ペースを超える利上げも示唆したらしい。

政策金利1.0%とFRBの3.5〜3.75%の差はまだ大きいけど、利上げ期待を受けて9月3日に円は1か月ぶりの高値まで戻した。
円高は円建ての金価格には下押し材料になりそう。

▶ 「利回り上昇はAIブームの反映」、財政危機説を否定（Nouriel Roubini、2026-09-06）
ルービニ氏は債券利回りの上昇について、AIブームが牽引する成長期待の表れであって財政危機のサインじゃないと述べた。
AI投資は設備投資と潜在成長率の底上げにつながるとして、AIバブルへの懸念もそこまでないとしてる。

高金利がしばらく続くとすれば、金にとっては逆風って話になりそう。

▶ 国内金価格は69万円台で推移、雇用統計と円高が重し（Nikkei Commodity、2026-09-06）
国内の金スポット価格は69万5,064円/オンス前後で推移してるみたい。
米雇用統計の上振れによる利上げ観測と、円高進行がどちらも押し下げ材料になってる。
銀は66.17ドルだった。

▶ 「もはや荒唐無稽じゃない」、米国による金準備押収への懸念（Paul Krugman、2026-09-06）
クルーグマン氏は、米国がニューヨーク連銀に保管する各国の金準備を押収するかもしれないという懸念は、もはや荒唐無稽とは言えないと論じてる。
オランダは3〜8月にかけて金86トンをニューヨークやオタワからロンドンへ移送済みで、フランスもすでにパリへ移管してる。

現政権下での法の支配の低下が、各国が金をニューヨークから引き揚げる理由になってるって見方らしい。

quote:
Thanks to AI these conundrums are a little easier to have a fresh perspective on.

Nominal house prices (+46%) and M3 (+42%) have tracked each other almost exactly over five and a half years. That's the unremarkable part — Australian housing is essentially a leveraged claim on credit growth, and broad money is credit growth. Housing hasn't outrun the money supply; it's kept pace with it.
Gold is the outlier. It roughly doubled the other two, then went vertical through 2025 (+53% in AUD that year alone) and peaked around A$7,700/oz in January 2026 before an ~16% correction.
Priced in gold, the median Australian house has lost about 43% since 2021 — from ~260 oz to ~148 oz. Most of that happened in 2025. The 2021 boom actually looked real in gold terms (houses gained on gold that year); everything since has been giving it back.
Caveats: the house-price series is reconstructed from Cotality's annual index changes anchored to the current median, so the intermediate points are approximations, not the published index. M3 monthly figures are interpolated between the RBA prints I could verify (Jan 2025 ~3,133bn, Jul 2026 ~3,512bn). Perth Mint publishes exact 30-June AUD gold prices if you want a cleaner FY-basis version, and the RBA's D3 table has the full M3 monthly series.

In other words the govt money printing has doubled everything from vovid.  Stop spending and show some austerity...

News Lead Up

Crypto peak!?

The crypto market has broken out of its consolidation

Market Overview

The cryptocurrency market has risen by almost 8% over the past 24 hours to $2.37T, reaching its highest level since early June. The initial momentum came on the back of news that the US Treasury was supporting the debt market. This relatively small but timely move signalled that the government is monitoring the situation in the debt markets, spurring demand for risk assets. The rally was then fuelled by a wave of short-covering, following weeks of extremely narrow trading.

Bitcoin reached $70K, posting a 9% rally over 8 hours during the US trading session. As the new day began, the leading cryptocurrency retreated slightly to $69.6K. On Monday, BTC consolidated above the 50-day moving average, and by Wednesday, it had already tested the 200-day MA. As expected, the market’s long-compressed spring snapped back, catching those who had been range-trading and those who had been building short positions on the rise off guard. If Bitcoin does not quickly lose its recent gains, it will be a significant sign that a bull market has begun, much like in October 2023 or March 2020.

Ethereum recorded an even more impressive breakout, showing an 18% gain over 24 hours at its peak. Having risen to $2.25K, the second-largest cryptocurrency is trading near its April–May highs, having broken above its 200-day moving average and away from a long-term support line that has risen from around $1.75K to $1.9K over the past 8 months. The next significant level where the coin may face resistance to further gains appears to be the $2.5K–$2.8K range. (FxPro)

News Lead Up

Aug 20

Cryptos

Crypto has reached May’s max, aiming higher

Market Overview

The cryptocurrency market has risen by 0.75% over the past 24 hours to $2.68T, trading close to this week’s highs. Judging by intraday movements, the market is poised for further growth, as investors actively buy up local price dips. While the major cryptocurrencies have stabilised near their highs of recent months, buyer interest has shifted towards altcoins. Over the past day, the top gainers were Official Trump (+27%), Uniswap (+6.7%) and Solana (+6.3%). The biggest fallers were SushiSwap and IOTA (both down 2.3%) and Immutable (down 1.8%).

The sentiment index continues to hover just below the extreme-greed threshold, a level we last saw consistently from May to August last year. Spikes in the indicator in January and May were short-lived or failed to sustain levels above the 50-mark. We are therefore observing an important confirmatory signal of a shift in sentiment from bearish to bullish.

At the time of writing, Bitcoin is trading just below $80K, but during a period of reduced liquidity ahead of the start of the Asian session, the price spiked to near $81.5K, setting a new high over the past three and a half months. It was near these levels in May that the leading cryptocurrency formed a local rebound peak, so it is logical to expect consolidation at this level for 5–10 days, though it may take longer. The next stage of growth is expected to be the $90K region, where BTC has held steady for two months since the end of November last year.

News Background

Inflows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs have continued for eight consecutive trading sessions. During this period, investors have poured $2.8 billion into the funds, bringing the total inflow to $54.7 billion.

Concerns over US government debt are driving investors towards alternative savings options such as Bitcoin and gold, according to BlackRock. The recent rise in BTC is consistent with the cryptocurrency's cyclical nature.

The US authorities have transferred 24,408 BTC, worth approximately $1.91 billion, from a wallet containing assets confiscated from the bankrupt crypto exchange FTX. The transfer of assets does not necessarily indicate an impending sell-off, though Arkham does not rule it out.

The UK has announced plans for the Bank of England to facilitate the development of payment systems and new forms of digital money, including stablecoins. The regulator’s primary focus will remain on financial stability.

A survey by the National Institute on Retirement Security found that 53% of Americans oppose employers offering cryptocurrency as a means of saving for retirement. Only 6% of those surveyed fully support using such an asset to build up retirement savings.

Summary: The crypto market is at $2.68T (+0.75%), with BTC at $80K and altcoins rising. ETF inflows hit $2.8 billion over 8 sessions, while BlackRock views BTC as a hedge against US debt risks.

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.
